record.paper_title: Jet tomography in heavy-ion collisions - Challenges, Results, and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Soft-Hard Event Engineering and background fluctuations
record.original_question: In Soft-Hard Event Engineering for heavy-ion collisions, how do the low-pT background geometry and event-by-event fluctuations, specifically selections by e2 eccentricity within a centrality class, affect hard high-pT jet observables such as the nuclear modification factor RAA and high-pT elliptic flow v2?

evidence.quote: To further study the impact of the background on the high-pT elliptic flow, in particular the impact of the e2-eccentricity selection (determining the centrality of a collision) within a given centrality class, we have recently started to compare various selected soft (low-pT background) and hard (high-pT jet) events [59].

Fig. 3 shows that there is almost no difference between the event-by-event and smoothed initial conditions for the nuclear modification factor. Thus, RAA is independent of the e2-eccentricity distribution of the background medium. Fig. 4 demonstrates that the high-pT v2 is proportional to the low-pT v2 (which is the largest for the top 1% e2 events) and that the width of the low-pT v2-distribution influences the high-pT v2. Besides that, the event-by-event fluctuations enhance the high-pT v2, depending on the e2-eccentricity selection.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions modeled as a two-component (soft + hard) system. The soft sector describes a low transverse-momentum (low-pT) bulk medium whose transverse geometry in a given centrality class fluctuates event by event; quantify its azimuthal asymmetry by the second-order eccentricity

  e2 = |∫ d²x_⊥ ρ(x_⊥) x_⊥² e^{2iφ}| / ∫ d²x_⊥ ρ(x_⊥) x_⊥²,

where ρ is the initial energy-density distribution in the transverse plane. Within a fixed centrality class, sub-classes of events are selected according to their value of e2 (e.g., the top 1% in e2, or events near the mean of the e2 distribution). The hard sector consists of high-pT partons that traverse the medium and lose energy according to a jet-energy-loss model, producing observable jets characterized by

  – the nuclear modification factor R_AA(pT) = (dN^{AA}/dpT) / (N_coll · dN^{pp}/dpT),
  – the high-pT elliptic flow v2(pT) = ⟨cos[2(φ − Ψ_RP)]⟩ of the hard hadron/jet distribution,

while the soft bulk also produces a low-pT v2.

Within this Soft-Hard Event Engineering framework, determine quantitatively how the choice of low-pT background — specifically (a) using event-by-event fluctuating initial conditions versus a smoothed (event-averaged) initial condition, and (b) restricting to e2-selected sub-samples within a fixed centrality class — affects:

  (i) the high-pT nuclear modification factor R_AA(pT), and
  (ii) the high-pT elliptic flow v2(pT), including its dependence on the mean and width of the low-pT v2 distribution induced by the e2 selection.

In particular, establish whether R_AA is sensitive or insensitive to the e2-eccentricity distribution of the background, and characterize the proportionality (or other functional dependence) between high-pT v2 and low-pT v2 across e2-selected sub-classes, as well as the role of event-by-event background fluctuations in enhancing the high-pT v2.
artifact.status_search_result: Studies of Soft-Hard Event Engineering have established (within specific energy-loss models) that R_AA is essentially independent of e2-eccentricity selection within a centrality class, while high-pT v2 is approximately proportional to low-pT v2 and is enhanced by event-by-event fluctuations. These qualitative findings are reproduced in subsequent analyses, but a complete, model-independent quantitative description across all observables and energies remains incomplete, so the broader problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Jet tomography in heavy-ion collisions - Challenges, Results, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: R_AA is independent of the e2-eccentricity distribution of the background medium; high-pT v2 is proportional to the low-pT v2 and event-by-event fluctuations enhance the high-pT v2.
status_evidence.claim: Within the soft-hard event engineering framework, the qualitative answers to (i) and (ii) are established for the studied energy-loss model.
